selectionReason: Maine is not yet represented in the route inventory and offers unusually strong public-access and managed-camping evidence across wilderness, moving-water, tidal-transition, and urban-edge trip types. DACF publishes a statewide launch inventory, while its public-land program documents the Allagash, Penobscot River Corridor, and other classic canoe systems.

existingCoverageAudit.overlapFindings: No pre-existing Maine route IDs, slugs, or route families were found before the expansion. The three lower-Allagash legs were checked against the official mileage chart; Allagash Falls to Twin Brook and Twin Brook to Allagash Village are intentionally combined into one 14-mile operational card to avoid a duplicate short leg. The second and third batches partition Penobscot, Kennebec, Androscoggin, Aroostook, Saco, St. John, St. Croix, Moosehead, Flagstaff, Pleasant, and Piscataquis into non-identical access pairs; lake cards remain planning itineraries rather than surveyed shoreline tracks.
